title: QUIC RFC 9000 Preferred Address Validation and Cutover Work Item
summary: Add focused requirement-home proof and trace ownership for preferred-address candidate validation, PATH_CHALLENGE response, and validated preferred-address non-probing cutover.
planned_changes:
- Add direct positive proof that the chosen preferred address remains a candidate path until validation succeeds.
- Add direct positive proof that a protected PATH_CHALLENGE on the preferred-address candidate path receives a matching PATH_RESPONSE on that path.
- Add edge proof that validated IPv6 preferred-address selection also becomes the exclusive non-probing send path.
- Link the S9P6P2-0008 through S9P6P2-0010 requirements to dedicated architecture, work-item, and verification artifacts.
- Regenerate QUIC requirement coverage triage and run focused verification.
verification_plan: Run the focused S9P6P2-0008/0009/0010 requirement-home filter, run a Release build, run the full Release no-build solution test suite, regenerate QUIC requirement coverage triage, validate SpecTrace JSON, and check the diff for whitespace errors.
out_of_scope: Complete S9P6P2 closure for requirements outside 0008 through 0010.
Multipath scheduling or multiple active outbound paths.
A new largest-packet-number policy seam beyond the current runtime path-validation promotion event.
completion_notes: Completed as a focused proof and trace slice over the existing preferred-address candidate-path and path-validation runtime behavior.
